title: Slowly changing dimensions and temporal joins
summary: Distinguish correcting current data from preserving historical context.

claims.text: SCD type 1 overwrites a value; type 2 keeps time-based versions of a member.

levels.overview: A fictional customer moves from North to South: should old sales move too?
levels.architecture: Contrast current-state lookup with a business-key plus validity-period lookup.
levels.detail: Inspect two customer versions and half-open validity intervals. Reject overlapping intervals for a claimed single-version match.

example.input: Customer C1 changes region on 2026-07-01; one sale is dated June and another August.
steps: Create a North version valid before July.
Create a South version valid from July.
Match each sale to the version valid on its date.
example.output: June maps to North and August to South.
limits: This is an original teaching example.
Do not infer that an owner dataset implements SCD2 from column names.

alternatives.label: Type 1
alternatives.whenToConsider: Use when current truth or correction is the intended question.

alternatives.label: Type 2
alternatives.whenToConsider: Use when the selected attributes require historical perspective.

interview.question: Why can joining facts to the current customer row change the meaning of historical results?
